name: sayings
description: SAYings — offline-first household finance and budgeting PWA you host on your own Cloudflare account

scripts.deploy: npm run db:backup && npm run db:migrate && vite build && node scripts/check-bundle.mjs && wrangler deploy -c "$(node scripts/wrangler-config.mjs --built)"
scripts.db:migrate: wrangler d1 migrations apply DB --remote -c "$(node scripts/wrangler-config.mjs --path)"
scripts.typecheck: tsc -p tsconfig.json && tsc -p tsconfig.worker.json && tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json && tsc -p tsconfig.node.json
scripts.verify: npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test

//deploy: Backup, then migrate, then ship. The order is deliberate: an installation may be several versions behind and about to apply four migrations at once, with nobody but its owner able to fix it. Migrations reference the DB *binding*, not the database name, because the name differs per installation.

DB.description: Your household's ledger: accounts, categories, transactions, budgets and exchange rates. Nobody else can read it.

FILES.description: Holds the nightly database snapshots and any receipt photos. Retention is 30 daily and 12 monthly.

TEAM_DOMAIN.description: Your Cloudflare Zero Trust team domain, with the scheme — `https://your-team.cloudflareaccess.com`. Found in Zero Trust → Settings. Leave as CHANGEME for now: the app shows you where to get it after deploying.

POLICY_AUD.description: The Access application's **Audience (AUD) Tag**, which only exists once you have created the Access policy. Leave as CHANGEME for now — the app will walk you through it.

UPDATE_CHECK.description: `on` asks GitHub once a night whether a newer release exists, so Settings can tell you. Set to `off` to make no outbound requests at all. Nothing is ever sent anywhere either way.
